name: Trollgädda
body:
TROLLGÄDDA
CR 7

This sharp toothed predatory fish of astonishing size has an elongated dappled tawny body. A green shrub-like growth sprouts upward from just behind its head.

XP 3,200
N Huge magical beast (aquatic)
Init +6; Senses darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision; Perception +15

DEFENSE

AC 20, touch 10, flat-footed 18 (+2 Dex, +10 natural, –2 size)
hp 85 (9d10+36); fast healing 2
Fort +10, Ref +8, Will +6

OFFENSE

Speed swim 60 ft.
Melee bite +16 (2d6+13/19–20 plus grab)
Space 15 ft.; Reach 10 ft.
Special Attacks death curse, swallow whole (2d4 bludgeoning damage, AC 15, 8 hp)

STATISTICS

Str 28, Dex 14, Con 19, Int 2, Wis 13, Cha 11
Base Atk +9; CMB +20 (+24 grapple); CMD 32
Feats Improved Critical (bite), Improved Initiative, Iron Will, Power Attack, Skill Focus (Perception)
Skills Perception +15, Swim +21
SQ angler’s fortune, hold breath, size reduction

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Angler’s Fortune (Su)

A creature that catches a trollgädda and then releases it is rewarded with a +5 luck bonus to a single Craft or Profession check each day for a year.

Death Curse (Su)

A creature that kills a trollgädda must succeed at a DC 18 Will save or take a –5 penalty to all Craft and Profession checks, as well as any skill checks made to create or repair magic items. This is a curse effect and the save DC is Constitutionbased.

Hold Breath (Ex)

A trollgädda can hold its breath for a number of minutes equal to its Constitution score before it risks suffocation.

Size Reduction (Su)

As a swift action, a trollgädda can magically shrink its body to Large size which functions as reduce animal, or reduce itself to Medium size as if affected by the harmless form spell. This transformation is fluid and instinctive, allowing the trollgädda to shift between smaller and larger sizes as needed. The trollgädda (plural trollgäddor) is an aquatic supernatural fish with the form of a giant pike. The crest which sprouts up from behind the trollgädda’s head and neck bears a resemblance to a willow shrub but is actually part of the creature’s body and hints at its sacred connection to the forces of nature.

ECOLOGY

Environment cold and temperate fresh water
Organization solitary or pair
Treasure incidental

With a cunning yet playful nature these wild willful creatures can cause problems ranging from being nuisances to attacking people. The trollgädda may drag nets or boats away and are a danger to swimmers. They are even known overturn small boats and eat the occupants.

Some trollgäddor test themselves against fisherfolk by biting a fishing line and forcing the angler into a truly heroic test of strength and endurance.

Stories tell of a fisherman who caught a large, but seemingly normal-sized pike. As he carried it back to his house, it grew larger and heavier. Soon its size threatened to destroy his home until he helped the fish outside and it squirmed and flopped its way back into the water. Another tale tells of an enterprising villager who tried to catch a trollgädda using a thick rope for fishing line and a dead foal for bait. When the creature took the line, the villager tied the rope to a lakeside barn and went to get help. When they returned, they found the barn had been dragged into the lake.

Some trollgäddor are linked to the powerful water-spirits called sjörå (“Mistress of the Lake,”). These fey see them as favored pets and decorate them with bells, earning them the title skällgäddor (“bell pikes”). Anyone who harms these skällgäddor risks their mistress’s anger.
